atlas-ca.0128: Foreign degrees are checked formally for immigration and for regulated occupations: an Educational Credential Assessment from an organisation such as WES, ICAS or the University of Toronto’s Comparative Education Service shows a foreign degree is equal to a Canadian one, but it does not give a licence.
atlas-ca.0129: Regulated occupations require licensing in the province where you work; the CPA route asks for a recognised degree of at least 120 credit hours and a 70% average.
atlas-ca.0130: Employers recruit where they have ties: Shopify takes 40% of its interns from Waterloo and Waterloo’s pool draws more than 8,000 employers. Outside those channels, the pages read do not rank schools.
atlas-ca.0131: Co-op plays the part of dual study: Waterloo posts over 24,000 positions a year for its co-op students, but co-op is a feature of particular universities and programmes rather than a national system.
atlas-ca.0132: The federal public service had 345,282 employees in March 2026, down from 357,965 a year earlier, and Ottawa–Gatineau has 194,000 people in public administration; Budget 2025 aims for about 40,000 fewer positions by April 2029.
atlas-ca.0133: An employer can use the Global Skills Strategy, which aims to process eligible, complete work permit applications within 2 weeks for a Global Talent Stream job, but the applicant must apply from outside Canada and the job must be on the eligible list. The federal CSE takes only citizens. See Visas for the rules.
atlas-ca.0134: No photo, no date of birth; a short résumé in North American style. Job Bank says a photo is not the norm in Canada and can lower your chances, and advises leaving out age, marital status and religious or political views, and never giving your Social Insurance Number.
atlas-ca.0135: The government’s résumé guide limits the résumé to two pages, with the stress on recent experience and little space for jobs older than 15 years.
atlas-ca.0136: The Job Bank résumé guide does not address cover letters. In practice a short tailored letter is added when a posting invites one; no page read sets a rule.
atlas-ca.0137: Do not list references on the résumé; keep them on a separate sheet and give them only when asked. Choose former managers, and for newcomers international managers, professors or volunteer supervisors; ask permission first.
atlas-ca.0138: Applications do not ask for certified copies of diplomas; certified credential assessment is for immigration and licensing, and the CPA route checks credit hours and average through its own registration.
atlas-ca.0139: Ontario postings now state the pay or a range, so applicants are not asked to name a figure first; elsewhere Job Bank postings often show a range marked to be negotiated.
atlas-ca.0140: Employers generally need written, specific consent before a check. The common checks are criminal record (convictions in the RCMP database), education, employment and, rarely, credit; a Vulnerable Sector Check is for work with children, older people or people with disabilities.
atlas-ca.0141: Federal security roles go far beyond this: CSE says assessment and clearance can take 12 to 18 months, with a background check covering at least 10 years.
atlas-ca.0142: Formal channels work: Waterloo’s matching, the CPA campus rounds and the bank programmes are all applications, but a career office tells students that boards alone are not the most effective method.
atlas-ca.0143: Co-op and the post-graduation work permit come with a Canadian degree; hiring a new graduate from abroad needs a sponsored permit.
atlas-ca.0144: The faster Global Skills Strategy needs an online application made from outside Canada, and federal security roles require citizenship.
atlas-ca.0145: English, and French in Quebec and for many federal posts. Federal bilingual posts carry a three-letter language profile (reading, writing, speaking) at levels A, B or C, and Quebec firms with 25 to 49 employees must register with the French-language office from 1 June 2025.
atlas-ca.0146: Co-op matching is a short, scheduled sequence: employers post, students apply, interviews run over about two weeks, then both sides rank and the system matches them; interviews pause during reading week and holidays.
atlas-ca.0147: CPA firm rounds are concentrated in the fall, and students are responsible for each firm’s process and deadlines. Government processes are longer: FSWEP matches are followed by a test or interview, and CSE assessment and clearance can take 12 to 18 months.
atlas-ca.0148: Ontario employers that interview must tell the applicant within 45 days whether a hiring decision has been made, and must say in the posting whether AI is used to screen applicants.
atlas-ca.0149: The probation length is set in the offer letter. In the federal public service it averages 12 months for positions of more than a year, and notice during probation depends on the employee class (for example 2 weeks or 1 month).
atlas-ca.0150: Ontario’s statutory notice of termination applies after 3 months of continuous employment: 1 week before the first anniversary, 2 weeks after 1 year, then one more week for each further year of service to a maximum of 8 weeks.
atlas-ca.0151: An offer is negotiable in the private sector; where Ontario postings now carry a range of no more than $50,000, the offer is expected to sit inside it.
atlas-ca.0152: Few pages name sponsoring employers. The employer-side tool is the Global Talent Stream of the Global Skills Strategy: for a job needing a labour-market assessment (LMIA) the employer provides a contract, an offer letter and a positive LMIA issued through the stream; for an exempt job the employer pays a compliance fee, and only top-level and degree-level jobs (TEER 0 or 1) qualify.
atlas-ca.0153: Ask early: the 2-week target runs from a complete application made from outside Canada, family members must apply at the same time, and biometrics are due within 2 weeks of the instruction letter.
atlas-ca.0154: Some federal employers cannot sponsor at all: CSE hires only Canadian citizens, and FSWEP gives preference to citizens and permanent residents.
atlas-ca.0155: Official: the Government of Canada Job Bank (jobbank.gc.ca), GC Jobs for the federal public service, and Ontario Public Service Careers for summer posts. Students also use TalentEgg, Eluta, Indeed, Workopolis Campus, Magnet and the university’s own board.
atlas-ca.0156: University career offices run the co-op and campus rounds (WaterlooWorks at Waterloo; CPABC publishes information sessions and webinars every month), and employer sites carry the programmes: RBC, Scotiabank, and the Communications Security Establishment’s student page.
atlas-ca.0157: Sending a photo, date of birth or a long CV: Job Bank says the photo is not the norm and can lower your chances, and the résumé should stay within two pages.
atlas-ca.0158: Missing the fall window: CPABC says larger firms hire about a year ahead, with most activity from August to October, and each firm may set its own deadlines.
atlas-ca.0159: Leaving the federal route too late: CSE asks for an application about eight months before the start, and security clearance for students takes about six months.
atlas-ca.0160: Treating a degree assessment as a licence: an Educational Credential Assessment does not give a licence or a job, and regulated occupations need licensing in the province where you work.
atlas-ca.0161: The big-bank graduate pages read (RBC, Scotiabank) state no language level; Scotiabank’s careers site is offered in English, French and Spanish. Check the French requirement of Quebec roles separately.
atlas-ca.0162: The CPA route is run in the province’s own CPA body; the CPA Ontario conditions named by RBC (a recognised degree of 120 credit hours, a 70% average, qualifying courses) mention no language certificate.
atlas-ca.0163: Federal bilingual posts carry a profile of three letters (reading, writing, oral) up to level C; the test comes late in the appointment process, and imperative staffing, where the level must be met at appointment, is the norm.
atlas-ca.0164: Co-op software hiring runs in English at Waterloo; the pages read for Shopify and the banks’ technology programmes state no other language requirement.
atlas-ca.0165: Montréal’s AI sector (Mila, IVADO, Google and Meta research centres) sits in a province where businesses with 25 to 49 employees must register with the French-language office from 1 June 2025; the pages read state no level for AI roles.
atlas-ca.0166: CSE student positions are in Ottawa or by telework; the student page lists no language level, and applicants must be Canadian citizens for the clearance.
atlas-ca.0167: Co-op is linked to better outcomes in the C.D. Howe study reported by the University of Toronto: co-op graduates earn more and land jobs that better match their field.
atlas-ca.0168: Ivey’s MSc class of 2023/24 had an 85% offer rate and a median base of C$75,000, with 30% going into financial services.
atlas-ca.0169: No page read gives a return-offer rate for Canadian co-op or bank programmes, and no recent-graduate unemployment series for 2026 was found.
atlas-ca.0171: Canada caps study permits at 408,000 in 2026. Bachelor’s and college students need a provincial attestation letter first; master’s and PhD students at public institutions have been exempt since 1 January 2026. In Québec you also need a CAQ.
atlas-ca.0172: Off campus you may work 24 hours a week in term and full time in scheduled breaks; going over can cost you your status.
atlas-ca.0174: CAD 23,448 a year, plus first-year tuition and CAD 2,000 for travel
atlas-ca.0178: Co-op placements and IEC International Co-op
